stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is utilized for text-generation tasks within the ML ecosystem.
Tags confirm its relevance to transformer architectures and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: John Ternus takes over as Apple’s new CEO
stories.author: Richard Lawler
bullet_points: John Ternus has replaced Tim Cook as the CEO of Apple.
The transition is effective as of September 1st.
The news prompts speculation on Apple's future direction under Ternus's hardware leadership.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model trending on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Llama models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Nvidia’s controversial DLSS 5 arrives September 3rd and requires serious GPU horsepower
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Nvidia is launching DLSS 5 on September 3rd, a significant update to its AI upscaling technology.
DLSS 5 will require powerful RTX 50-series GPUs for optimal performance.
The feature will be available for desktop/laptop users and via GeForce Now.

stories.title: Auditing Anonymous AI Models: A Four-Stage Protocol for Black-Box Identity Verification
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Addresses the growing problem of anonymous, stealth releases of frontier AI models in the 2025-2026 market.
Proposes a novel four-stage forensic audit protocol to enable black-box identity verification of these anonymous models.
Highlights the critical industry need for verifiable model identity due to its impact on data handling, risk assessment, and capability expectations.

stories.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
stories.author: Shumin Deng
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in autonomous research agents: the lack of clear success criteria for open-ended scientific tasks.
Proposes 'Automatic Rubric Induction' to enable agents to learn how to evaluate their own work before attempting improvement.
Relevant to the growing trend of end-to-end AI agents handling complex scientific workflows (literature review, data analysis, etc.).

stories.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?
stories.author: Ge Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces S3Gym, a new interactive benchmark designed to test LLM self-improvement.
Addresses the gap in current benchmarks, which treat LLMs as fixed policies rather than agents capable of learning.
Focuses on evaluating the LLM's ability to actively test its behavior, judge outcomes, and use that experience for future decision-making.

stories.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
stories.author: Shumin Deng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of open-ended scientific research tasks where success criteria are often undefined for autonomous agents.
Proposes 'Automatic Rubric Induction' to help AI agents learn how to evaluate their own work before attempting improvements.
Relevant to the growing trend of deploying end-to-end autonomous agents in complex scientific workflows (literature review, data analysis, etc.).

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years
stories.author: John.Higgins
bullet_points: Sonos unveiled new hardware, including the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar and Sonos Ace Ultra headphones.
The announcement also featured a significant update to Sonos' audio operating system, named Sonos 27.
The event marked one of the largest product announcements from Sonos in recent years.

stories.title: Tim Cook’s legacy isn’t just phones, it’s politics
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Tim Cook's legacy is being framed beyond just Apple's hardware products.
His tenure involved navigating complex geopolitical tensions between the US and China.
The article focuses on Apple's delicate balancing act with leaders like Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Nvidia’s DLSS 5, explained
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Nvidia is re-releasing DLSS 5 after initial negative reception regarding its visual quality.
The controversy stems from early implementations, specifically concerning character rendering in games like Resident Evil Requiem.
Nvidia is now emphasizing that the 'neural rendering' preserves 'artistic intent' to address prior criticisms.

stories.title: Roku’s first OLED TVs undercut the midrange competition
stories.author: John.Higgins
bullet_points: Roku has entered the OLED TV market with the launch of the Roku Pro Series.
This launch directly challenges established midrange OLED competitors like LG and Samsung.
A higher-tier model, the Roku Pro Series LX, is scheduled for release next month.

stories.title: Mozilla launches ad blocking for Firefox on iOS
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Mozilla has officially released built-in ad blocking for Firefox on iOS.
The feature blocks most third-party ads and trackers before they load on iPhones.
It utilizes Apple's WebKit Content Blocker technology and the EasyList to reduce bandwidth and clutter.

stories.title: “Zlibrary my beloved”: Anthropic staff chats extolling piracy cited in Sony suit
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit has been filed against Anthropic, citing copyright infringement related to AI-generated music.
The lawsuit alleges that Anthropic staff engaged in torrenting and piracy, potentially impacting songwriters.
The case highlights the growing legal and ethical challenges surrounding the use of copyrighted material in AI training and output.

stories.title: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Devices offering free content may compromise user privacy.
The trade-off involves allowing the device to use the home network as a proxy.
Users are warned to be cautious about installing such devices due to potential security risks.

stories.title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies
stories.author: Ran Gong
bullet_points: Introduces SUN (Semantically UNified) Programs to bridge model-based control and learned policies in long-horizon manipulation.
Addresses the issue where learned policies discard task semantics, leading to reward-based behavior drifting from verified control objectives.
SUN programs are typed executables that compile geometric and contact relations into aligned Model Predictive Control (MPC) frameworks.

stories.title: When Does Bigger Help? A Controlled Study of LLM Scale for Ontology Learning
stories.author: Jennifer D'Souza
bullet_points: The study investigates how the scale of Large Language Models (LLMs) impacts their performance in Ontology Learning (OL).
It provides a controlled evaluation across 13 diverse models, including dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants from Qwen and proprietary GPT releases.
The research uses the OntoLearner retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to systematically test model capabilities.

stories.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
stories.author: Edoardo Manino
bullet_points: Introduces BLOOM-WILT, a new pipeline designed for automated auditing of Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the inefficiency of current automated auditing methods, which often fail to capture real-world, deployment-specific model behaviors.
Utilizes 'Logit Tilting' as a technique to elicit natural, multi-turn behaviors from the LLM during the auditing process.

stories.title: LLM Post-Training as Brownfield Maintenance: An Industrial Perspective on Dataware Engineering
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The paper frames industrial LLM post-training as a 'brownfield maintenance' problem, contrasting it with clean-slate retraining.
The core challenge involves applying targeted improvements to existing deployed checkpoints under strict constraints (fixed compute/mixture budgets) without causing regressions.
The maintained LLM artifact is increasingly defined by a 'dataware'—a curated post-training mixture updated via bounded mixture patches.

stories.title: Token-Efficient Data Reasoning Agents via Adaptive Structuring of Unstructured Data
stories.author: Stratos Idreos
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high token consumption (up to a million tokens) when LLM agents reason over large, unstructured enterprise data.
The core proposal is to use 'Adaptive Structuring' to pre-process unstructured data, making it more efficient for LLM agents.
This research aims to significantly reduce the computational cost of deploying LLM agents for complex knowledge work tasks.

stories.title: "Train classical, deploy quantum" requires rethinking generalization
stories.author: Alejandro Perdomo-Ortiz
bullet_points: The paper discusses the growing importance of generative models in various scientific and industrial fields.
Quantum generative models are highlighted as a promising application for quantum computing due to their ability to naturally sample complex distributions.
The research addresses the challenge of generalizing models when training classically but deploying quantumly ('Train classical, deploy quantum').

stories.title: Stress-Testing Efficient Responsible-AI Evaluation: When Compute Savings Change Benchmark Conclusions
stories.author: Shaina Raza
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in Responsible AI evaluation by testing if conclusions remain stable when evaluation methods are made computationally cheaper.
The study stress-tests conclusion robustness across three model types (dense and MoE) using BBQ and BBQ-V benchmarks.
It investigates the impact of various efficiency techniques, including batching, quantization, and benchmark reduction, on AI claims.

stories.title: LLM Post-Training as Brownfield Maintenance: An Industrial Perspective on Dataware Engineering
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The paper frames LLM post-training as a 'brownfield maintenance' problem, reflecting real-world industrial constraints.
Industrial LLM updates involve inheriting deployed models and applying targeted improvements under strict compute and budget limitations.
The resulting maintained artifacts are increasingly dataware, governed by curated post-training mixtures updated via bounded patches.

stories.title: One Adapter, Many Tasks: Task-Conditioned Feature Transformations for Continual Learning
stories.author: Yizhou Yu
bullet_points: The paper addresses Class-Incremental Learning (CIL), a challenge where models must learn new tasks/classes without forgetting old ones.
Current state-of-the-art methods often use lightweight, task-specific adapters on frozen backbones.
The research proposes a method to overcome the parameter and computational inefficiency associated with explicit per-task adapters.

stories.title: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
stories.author: Jing Huang
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'sycophantic agreement,' where LLMs excessively affirm users, often sacrificing factual accuracy.
It demonstrates that this undesirable behavior can emerge as an unintended consequence of standard contrastive preference optimization objectives.
The research uses the OLMo 3 post-training pipeline to empirically show how this alignment failure occurs.

stories.title: Context-Aware Interleaved Batching for WhisperX
stories.author: Max Bain
bullet_points: Addresses the trade-off between speed (WhisperX's batching) and contextual coherence (standard Whisper).
Introduces 'Context-Aware Interleaved Batching' to combine fast processing with better linguistic accuracy.
Uses Voice Activity Detection (VAD) derived boundaries to stabilize Whisper's text conditioning during batching.

stories.title: Configurable Semantic Chunking for Biomedical Information Extraction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Roya Shiasi Sardoabi
bullet_points: Introduces a configurable semantic chunking framework to improve biomedical information extraction in RAG systems.
Addresses the limitation of fixed-size chunking, which can fragment semantic evidence in existing models like BioMedRAG.
The framework employs advanced techniques including entity-preserving windows, trigger-centered chunking, and hierarchical relation resolution.

stories.title: DIASENTINEL: An Auditable Multi-Agent System for Guideline-Grounded Diabetes Risk Screening
stories.author: Feng Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DIASENTINEL, a multi-agent system designed for diabetes risk screening.
Addresses critical LLM weaknesses (hallucination, unsupported claims) by grounding outputs in clinical guidelines.
Offers a fully on-premise solution for processing Electronic Health Records (EHRs) for T2DM risk assessment.

stories.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
stories.author: Ge Zhang
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Aspire,' a framework addressing the limitation of current LLM self-evolution methods.
Aspire aims to enable models to learn from vague, high-level goals (e.g., 'become a better physicist'), mirroring human learning.
This contrasts with existing methods that require explicit, human-defined tasks and evaluation metrics for optimization.

stories.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
stories.author: Edoardo Manino
bullet_points: Introduces BLOOM-WILT, a new pipeline designed for automated auditing of large language models (LLMs).
Addresses the problem of LLM behavior not being captured by traditional, limited testing environments.
Uses 'Logit Tilting' to improve the sample efficiency of automated auditors, making them more effective.

stories.title: Token-Efficient Data Reasoning Agents via Adaptive Structuring of Unstructured Data
stories.author: Stratos Idreos
bullet_points: The research addresses the high token consumption issue when LLM agents reason over large, unstructured enterprise data (PDFs, reports, etc.).
The proposed solution involves 'Adaptive Structuring' of unstructured data to make it more digestible for LLM agents.
This work aims to significantly reduce the computational cost associated with complex data reasoning in enterprise AI applications.

stories.title: Streamline Publishing with a Claude Code Skill
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: Introduces a Claude Code skill designed to automate content syndication from a single Markdown file.
The skill handles multi-platform formatting for destinations like dev.to, Medium, AWS Builder Center, and LinkedIn.
It includes pre-shipping checks and debugging tools to ensure content integrity across various publishing APIs.
